See migration and state preservation. New public addresses require a separate deployment; no renamed GitHub repository is claimed. Image: Python >=3.11 Image: Ed25519 + ML-DSA signing Image: MIT > 🌐 English · Русский · Español · Français · 中文 An agent that buys, sells or pays needs facts no model can make up: is this VAT number valid, who is this company, what was the euro rate that day, is this wallet on a sanctions list, and can I prove this document existed yesterday. SYMMARTYS answers each from the public record — the European Commission, GLEIF, the ECB, the U.S. Treasury, the EU, the UK and Bitcoin — and signs every answer together with where it came from, when, and the SHA-256 of what the source returned. Symmartys (συμμάρτυς): a joint or corroborating witness — a source-backed answer that another party can check. Since 0.2.0 it also answers the questions that come next: is this company in its national register, is its EORI number valid for customs, how old is the domain the shop runs on, which day is the fifth business day in Bavaria or on TARGET2 — and it gives agents two tools no model has: a web page captured as evidence (anchored in Bitcoin) and a timer, including a dead man's switch, that calls the agent back with a signed event. ## Capabilities Capability | Price | What it answers | Source --- | --- | --- | --- `symmartys.vat.check@v1` | $0.002 | Is this EU VAT number valid today? Name, address, time of the check — and, when you name your own VAT number as requester, VIES's consultation number: official proof of the check in your name | EU VIES `symmartys.lei.lookup@v1` | $0.001 | Who is this legal entity? By LEI (check digits verified locally) or by name (ranked candidates): legal name, jurisdiction, legal form, status, addresses, renewal, direct and ultimate parents | GLEIF (CC0) `symmartys.fx.rate@v1` | $0.001 | Euro reference rate for any pair on any date since 1999, the ECB day it is from, cross rates through the euro in Decimal, an amount rounded to the currency's minor units | ECB `symmartys.sanctions.screen@v1` | $0.002 | Is this wallet address or name on a public sanctions list? OFAC SDN (with ~1,050 digital-currency addresses), EU and UK lists (UN designations through them, each hit with its UN number), with each list's date and SHA-256 | OFAC · EU · UK `symmartys.timestamp.stamp@v1` | $0.001 | Anchor a SHA-256 digest in Bitcoin through the OpenTimestamps calendars; returns a standard `.ots` proof | OpenTimestamps `symmartys.timestamp.verify@v1` | $0.001 | Upgrade and verify a proof: confirmed when its result equals the Merkle root of the Bitcoin block header SYMMARTYS holds from the Bitcoin network itself (every header's proof of work checked, the chain agreed by two nodes) | Bitcoin `symmartys.web.capture@v1` | $0.003 | A web page as evidence: final URL, every redirect, the IP, status, key headers, the TLS certificate and the SHA-256 of the body (and the body, up to 512 KB); the record's SHA-256 is anchored in Bitcoin | the page itself · OpenTimestamps `symmartys.domain.rdap@v1` | $0.001 | Who registered this domain and when: created, expires, age in days, registrar, status, nameservers, DNSSEC — or `registered: false` | IANA bootstrap → the TLD's registry `symmartys.company.lookup@v1` | $0.001 | Is this company real and alive? By number or name: name, status, legal form, founding date, address, VAT number, and the register's own fields | Brønnøysund (NO) · SIRENE/RNE (FR) · ARES (CZ) · PRH (FI) · Companies House (GB, with the operator's key) `symmartys.eori.check@v1` | $0.002 | Is this EORI number valid for EU customs? Up to 10 at once; name and address where the operator consented | European Commission (EOS) `symmartys.calendar.check@v1` | $0.001 | Business days in ~250 countries (and regions) or on a market (TARGET2, NYSE, LSE…): holiday, next/previous business day, date + N business days, days between, a year's holidays | python-holidays (offline) `symmartys.timer.set@v1` | $0.002 | A signed POST to your https callback at a time, or a dead man's switch that fires unless you check in every N seconds | — `symmartys.timer.checkin@v1` · `.cancel@v1` · `.status@v1` | free | Keep a dead man's switch alive, cancel a timer, read its state (with the timer's token) | — `symmartys.sources@v1` | free | Every source's licence and attribution, the sanctions lists held now, the latest ECB day | — ## Trust, briefly * Evidence in every answer — the source URL, the time it was fetched and the SHA-256 of the bytes it returned, plus the source's licence and attribution. * Two signatures — the gateway's signed receipt (oracle-core, Ed25519, hybrid ML-DSA when `ORACLE_PQC=1`) and the request-bound `X-Provider-Signature` the hub verifies. * A source that cannot answer costs nothing — the answer is `ok:false`, and the hub debits nothing for `ok:false`: a member state's VAT registry that is down, sanctions lists not loaded or older than 48 h, fewer than two timestamp calendars, a block the header chain does not reach yet. * Outbound requests are allowlisted per source; redirects are followed by hand and only to that source's own hosts; bodies are size-capped. * The two capabilities that call a URL the caller names (web capture and timer callbacks) reach public addresses only: http(s) on ports 80/443, every address of the name checked (no loopback, private, link-local, CGNAT or metadata ranges), the connection pinned to the checked address, every redirect checked again, and at most 20 captures of one host per minute. ## Examples H=https://symmartys.modelmarket.dev inv() { curl -s -X POST $H/ai-market/v2/invoke -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$1"; } inv '{"capability_id":"symmartys.vat.check@v1","input":{"vat":"NL004495445B01","requester_vat":"DE811569869"}}' inv '{"capability_id":"symmartys.lei.lookup@v1","input":{"name":"Deutsche Bank"}}' inv '{"capability_id":"symmartys.fx.rate@v1","input":{"base":"USD","quote":"JPY","date":"2026-10-11","amount":"100"}}' inv '{"capability_id":"symmartys.sanctions.screen@v1","input":{"address":"0x…"}}' inv '{"capability_id":"symmartys.timestamp.stamp@v1","input":{"digest":"'"$(sha256sum contract.pdf | cut -d' ' -f1)"'"}}' inv '{"capability_id":"symmartys.web.capture@v1","input":{"url":"https://shop.example/terms"}}' inv '{"capability_id":"symmartys.domain.rdap@v1","input":{"domain":"shop.example"}}' inv '{"capability_id":"symmartys.company.lookup@v1","input":{"country":"FR","number":"552032534"}}' inv '{"capability_id":"symmartys.eori.check@v1","input":{"eori":"CZ00177041"}}' inv '{"capability_id":"symmartys.calendar.check@v1","input":{"market":"XECB","add_business_days":5}}' inv '{"capability_id":"symmartys.timer.set@v1","input":{"callback":"https://agent.example/hook","deadman_seconds":3600,"payload":{"release":"escrow-7"}}}' Through the hub, the same calls are paid and receipted: `POST https://modelmarket.dev/ai-market/v2/invoke` with `"product_id":"symmartys"`. ### VAT: the consultation number VIES issues a consultation number only to a valid EU VAT number named as requester. It is the requester's proof, kept by the requester: pass your own number as `requester_vat` and the consultation number in the answer is evidence, in your name, that you checked your counterparty at `checked_at`. Without it the check is still made; the answer says how to get the number. ### FX: which day A rate "on" a date is the latest ECB publication on or before it, and the answer names that day (`ecb_date`): a Sunday is priced at Friday's rate, visibly. A currency the ECB stopped quoting (RUB since March 2022) is refused rather than answered with a years-old rate. ### Sanctions: a lookup, not a determination A wallet is matched exactly (EVM and bech32 addresses case-insensitively). A name is matched as a set of words — order, case, accents and legal forms ignored ("DOE, John" is "John Doe"), a word within a typo counts 0.9 and never reads as the same name, and every asked word found in a longer name (a patronymic, a middle name) still matches. The default threshold is 0.85; each hit says which name matched and its score. A hit is a reason to look closer; a miss is not a clearance. Names collide and aliases are incomplete. Every answer says so, and names the lists it used with their publication dates and SHA-256. An outdated list is refused, not used. UN designations come through the UK and EU lists. The UN Security Council's own file carries no reuse licence, so SYMMARTYS does not read it. The UK Sanctions List (Open Government Licence v3.0) gives every UN designation the UK implements its UN reference number, as the EU file does for some: a hit carries `un_ref`, and `lists: ["UN"]` screens only the UK and EU entries that have one. On 2026-10-17 the three lists together held all 1010 UN entries (991 by UN number in the UK list, the rest by name in the EU and OFAC lists). The newest UN decisions reach them with the delay the UK and the EU take to implement them, usually days. ### Timestamps sequenceDiagram autonumber participant A as Agent participant E as SYMMARTYS participant C as OpenTimestamps calendars participant B as Bitcoin nodes (P2P, ×2) A->>E: stamp {digest} E->>E: sha256(digest ‖ 16 random bytes) — calendars never see the digest E->>C: submit to all four, at least two must accept C-->>E: pending attestations E-->>A: .ots proof (pending) Note over C: a few hours later the calendars' aggregate
transaction is mined in a Bitcoin block A->>E: verify {digest, proof} E->>C: upgrade at each calendar the proof names (allowlisted only) C-->>E: path to the block E->>B: getheaders — the whole chain, kept and refreshed B-->>E: every header's proof of work and difficulty checked, a second node agrees E->>E: proof result == header Merkle root E-->>A: confirmed · existed no later than the block time · upgraded proof The proof is a standard OpenTimestamps file: it verifies with any OpenTimestamps client, without SYMMARTYS. The reference example (`hello-world.txt`) verifies to block 358 391, 2015-05-28. ### Web capture: what the page said SYMMARTYS fetches the page once, as a browser would, and returns a `record`: the URL asked, the final URL, every redirect with its status and IP, the time, the status, the headers that say what the page was (content type, length, `Last-Modified`, `ETag`, `Date`, `Server`…), the TLS certificate the server presented (subject, issuer, validity, names, SHA-256 of the certificate), the page title and `body_sha256`. The body itself comes back as `body_b64` when it is 512 KB or less (the cap for a page is 5 MB). `record_sha256` is the SHA-256 of the record as JSON with sorted keys and compact separators, and it is anchored in Bitcoin through OpenTimestamps — verify it later with `symmartys.timestamp.verify@v1`. A 404 is a capture (that is what the page said); a host that cannot be reached, or a certificate that does not verify, costs nothing. ### Timers and the dead man's switch sequenceDiagram autonumber participant A as Agent participant E as SYMMARTYS participant C as Agent callback (https) A->>E: timer.set {callback, deadman_seconds: 3600, payload} E-->>A: timer_id + token (once) loop while the agent is alive A->>E: timer.checkin {timer_id, token} E-->>A: due_at moved 3600 s ahead end Note over A: the agent stops E->>C: POST {event, signature} — Ed25519 (+ ML-DSA) over the event C-->>E: 2xx (else retried after 1, 5, 30 min) `at` (an ISO time with zone) or `after_seconds` sets a one-off call instead. The event carries the timer id, kind, due and fired times, the attempt and your payload (up to 4 KB); the signature is SYMMARTYS's key from its signed manifest, over the event as JSON with sorted keys and compact separators. The token is kept only as its SHA-256. Timers live at most 90 days, in one SQLite file in SYMMARTYS's data volume. ### Company registers, EORI, domains, business days * Company registers answer from the register itself: Norway's Brønnøysund Register Centre (NLOD 2.0), France's SIRENE and national register through the State's open API (Licence Ouverte 2.0), the Czech ARES, Finland's PRH (CC BY 4.0) and — where the operator has set `COMPANIES_HOUSE_API_KEY`, a free key — the UK's Companies House (OGL v3.0); without the key GB is not offered. Numbers are checked locally first (Norwegian, Czech and Finnish check digits; a French SIRET is reduced to its SIREN). Statuses: active, ceased/dissolved/deleted, bankrupt, in liquidation, in re-organisation. * EORI comes from the European Commission's EOS service; "not valid" is an answer. * RDAP is asked only at the servers IANA's bootstrap file names for the TLD (https only); a subdomain or URL is reduced to the registered name by asking the registry. Some country codes (`.de`, `.ru`…) publish no RDAP service yet — that is refused and costs nothing. * RDAP etiquette. Registries' terms forbid high-volume automated querying and repackaging, so SYMMARTYS asks one registry at most 30 times a minute, keeps each answer 24 hours (an hour for "not registered"; a cached answer says `cached: true` and keeps the original fetch time), and passes the registry's own notices — its terms of service among them — through as `registry_terms`. * Personal data. Registers list sole traders too, and their entries are personal data whatever the register's licence says. Every company answer carries `personal_data`: the purpose (verifying a counterparty), the basis (legitimate interest, GDPR Art. 6(1)(f)) and the retention (SYMMARTYS keeps no copy; its call log holds only a hash of the input). * Business days come from python-holidays compiled into SYMMARTYS: no network, nothing to go down; the answer names the library version, because a holiday declared after that release is not in it. ## Honest limits * VIES answers what the member state's registry answers at that moment; some states return no name or address. SYMMARTYS stores nothing. * GLEIF covers entities that have an LEI — many small companies do not. * Reference rates are for information, not dealing. * Sanctions screening is a lookup in three public lists, not legal advice or a compliance programme; other jurisdictions' lists are not included. * A timestamp proves existence no later than a block's time, not authorship. * A web capture shows what the server answered SYMMARTYS at that moment; another visitor, country or cookie may be shown another page. It is not a statement that the content is true. * Registers differ in what they publish; the registers of four countries (five with the UK key) are covered so far; Poland's KRS API did not answer when tried. * A timer is delivered at least once if the callback answers 2xx within four attempts; a receiver should treat a repeated `timer_id` with the same `due_at` as the same event. ## Run it # From the local aicom workspace root docker build -f symmartys/Dockerfile -t symmartys . docker run -d --name symmartys -p 127.0.0.1:9351:9351 -v symmartys-data:/data \ -e SYMMARTYS_PUBLIC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9351 symmartys curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9351/health In the aicom monorepo the same runs from its root with `SYMMARTYS_VOLUME_NAME=symmartys-data docker compose -f symmartys/docker-compose.yml up -d --build` (volume migration; fresh installs first run `docker volume create symmartys-data`). `SYMMARTYS_PUBLIC_URL` is the address buyers reach; it is written into the signed manifest. Production, from the aicom monorepo: `./scripts/deploy_symmartys.sh --remote ` serves it at `https://modelmarket.dev/providers/symmartys/` behind the existing nginx (one snippet, backed up, `nginx -t` before reload), keeps the running image as `symmartys:prev` and rolls back an unhealthy build. Steady memory ≈ 200 MB; the container is capped at 768 MB. It runs as uid 10001. Its branded deployment target is https://symmartys.modelmarket.dev/ — the landing for people at `/`, the same API for agents everywhere else (`deploy/nginx/symmartys.modelmarket.dev.conf`); the `/providers/symmartys/` path stays the address the hub federates with. Variable | Default | Meaning --- | --- | --- `SYMMARTYS_PUBLIC_URL` | `https://modelmarket.dev/providers/symmartys` | base URL in the manifest `SYMMARTYS_PORT` | `9351` | listen port `SYMMARTYS_RATE_LIMIT` | `120` | invokes per minute per client `SYMMARTYS_CORS_ORIGINS` | empty (no browser origin) | CORS allowlist `COMPANIES_HOUSE_API_KEY` | empty (GB not offered) | the operator's free Companies House API key `SYMMARTYS_TIMERS_DB` | `timers.sqlite` beside the signing key | where timers are kept `ORACLE_PQC` | `1` in compose | hybrid ML-DSA-65 signatures Tests: `pip install -e "vendor/oracle-core[pqc]" -e '.[dev]' && pytest` (in the monorepo: `-e ../oracles/core`) — 175 tests on excerpts of real answers, none reaching a live source; in the monorepo the signed canonical is also checked byte for byte against the hub's own function. ## Sources and licences Source | Licence | Attribution carried in answers --- | --- | --- EU VIES | European Commission reuse policy (Decision 2011/833/EU) | European Commission, VIES GLEIF | CC0 1.0 | Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation (GLEIF), CC0 ECB | reproduction with source acknowledgement | Source: European Central Bank OFAC SDN | U.S. Government work (public domain) | U.S. Department of the Treasury, OFAC EU Financial Sanctions Files | European Commission reuse policy | European Commission, FSF UK Sanctions List (FCDO) | Open Government Licence v3.0 | Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0 (UK Sanctions List, FCDO) OpenTimestamps | free public calendars | OpenTimestamps (opentimestamps.org) Bitcoin block headers | public chain data, fetched peer to peer | Bitcoin network EU EORI (EOS) | European Commission reuse policy | European Commission, EORI validation (EOS) Brønnøysund Register Centre | NLOD 2.0 | Brønnøysundregistrene, Enhetsregisteret (NLOD 2.0) API Recherche d'entreprises | Licence Ouverte 2.0 (Etalab) | DINUM, API Recherche d'entreprises (INSEE SIRENE, INPI RNE) ARES | Czech public administration open data | Ministerstvo financí ČR, ARES PRH / YTJ | CC BY 4.0 | Finnish Patent and Registration Office (PRH), YTJ open data Companies House (with a key) | Open Government Licence v3.0 | Contains public sector information from Companies House, OGL v3.0 RDAP | public registration data (RFC 9083) | IANA RDAP bootstrap and the TLD registry python-holidays | MIT | python-holidays (vacanza/holidays) Code: MIT — see LICENSE. (https://modelmarket.dev/blog/emberline-was-one-fire-desk-then-we-built-four-more-and-still-no-risk-score/) citeturn78search1 [wordlim: 200] Published: last month; Crawled: 2 weeks ago; Emberline still lives at emberlinedesk.com. 17 Sep 2026 · 4 min read # Emberline was one fire desk. Then we built four more — and still no risk score. Last month I wrote that pretty fire maps are liars. Then I unzipped the sample and said the globe was never the product. People liked the refusal. Then they asked the question that usually ruins it: So when do you add flood? And ships? And a campus? And can it just be one score? No. Emberline was one desk. Now there are five. Same kernel. Five brands. None of them will sell you a blended “risk score.” ## The pretty lie, again Dashboards love a single number. Fire plus flood plus AIS plus the weather, stirred until it looks like a decision. That number is interior design. It photographs well. It does not survive a lawyer, an editor, or a Tuesday on a call. We already refused to draw a fire perimeter we were not given. We refused to paint a county blue around one river gage. The family rule is the same sentence, five times: Never one score. Image: Live Cite Desks family — five specialist products on one evidence rail The public host is a demo. Checkout is closed. We did not dress a brochure as a storefront. ## Five cards. Five origins. Each desk buys attested ATLAS / GAIA evidence and sells a named watch: a box a person owns, scheduled runs, a cite pack. The brand on the paper is the desk, not the rail. Desk | Watches | The refusal --- | --- | --- Emberline | FIRMS / EFFIS points + bounded weather | Not a perimeter. Not a forecast. Not an evacuation. Tideline | CAP warning and an in-situ gauge | Two lists. Not a flood model. Solrecord | Irradiance at one plant pin | Not yield. Not P50 / P90. Seamark | Fintraffic and Kystverket | FI ≠ NO. Not global AIS. Plinth | Weather, air, water on one named site | Separate lists. Not a BMS. Not a campus risk score. Image: Live family cards — Emberline, Tideline, Solrecord, Seamark, Plinth Five origins. The public host stays a demo; operators bring their own keys. Image: One kernel. Five independent brands. Never one blended number. ATLAS and GAIA sell the signed snapshot. The desk sells the watching. Emberline still lives at emberlinedesk.com. The other four keep their own origins on purpose. Same shop-window family. Different front doors. Different brand on the cover. ## What this is not (say it like you mean it) The family page says it on the door: DEMO. Not for sale. Checkout is closed. Live hub invokes are capped. SIM is never dressed as LIVE. It is not NASA / EFFIS / NOAA. It is not insurance. It is not 911. It is not “AI predicts the fire / the flood / the ship / the campus.” If you operate your own origin, you bring the keys. The public host is a reference you can fork and brand. We did not open a carnival. Image: Five refusals stamped on cream paper Print the refusal. Pretty maps invent shapes. Desks do not. ## If you only remember one sentence One kernel. Five brands. Never one risk score. Open the family: desk.modelmarket.dev. The first desk, if you missed it: pretty fire maps are liars. The zip, if you want the file: the globe was never the product. — Cite Desks — five specialist products on one evidence rail. Independent. Citeable. It says so on the page. We did not dress a demo as this morning’s live run. Image: Emberline sample evidence brief — CA Transmission Corridor, stamps on the paper Cream paper. Three stamps. A small table that says two new dots showed up and one got brighter. That is the whole movie. If a dot disappears, the brief does not yell “the fire went out.” Clouds exist. Sensors blink. Adults can live with that. The download is a cite pack — a zip, like keeping the hardware-store receipt in a kitchen drawer. Map of dots. Weather on a leash (only nearby, not “vibes”). A signed stamp for who printed this. Not “the sky is on fire, signed, God.” Image: Manila folder labeled CITE PACK on a walnut table The product is the file you can keep. The globe is just the shop window. ## What this desk is not (say it like you mean it) It is not 911. It is not an insurance quote.
